# TulipLot

> TulipLot is a browser dashboard that shows up to six live websites side by side in a fixed 3×2 grid, in one browser tab.

## Facts
- Try: 2 usable cells, no account. Free: 5 usable cells + 1 ad cell, $0. Premium: 6 cells, no ad, $4/month.
- Most sites embed live. Some need the optional TulipLot Companion (a Chrome extension). A few never embed and open in their own tab from the grid.
- Chrome-first. Public site: https://tuliplot.com/

- [Adding sites that refuse to be framed](https://tuliplot.com/guides/add-any-site/): Why some sites show "refused to connect" in a dashboard, and how the TulipLot Companion extension unlocks them safely, one site at a time.
- [Premium vs Free — what you get](https://tuliplot.com/guides/premium-vs-free/): Everything the free plan includes, exactly what $4/month adds, and what happens to your grid when you upgrade, downgrade, or cancel.
- [Why some sites won't load in a dashboard](https://tuliplot.com/guides/why-sites-wont-load/): "Refused to connect" isn't a bug in your dashboard. Here's what that message actually means, which sites do it, and what can and can't be done about it.

- [TulipLot vs start.me: widgets and links, or live sites?](https://tuliplot.com/blog/tuliplot-vs-start-me/): start.me builds a start page from bookmarks and widgets. TulipLot renders a fixed grid of real sites, live. How the two differ, and what each one costs.
- [TulipLot vs Toby: which one fits how you actually work?](https://tuliplot.com/blog/tuliplot-vs-toby/): Toby saves tabs you reopen later. TulipLot keeps a fixed grid of sites live at once. An honest look at both, with prices and free-plan limits.
- [TulipLot vs Workona: project spaces or a live grid?](https://tuliplot.com/blog/tuliplot-vs-workona/): Workona sorts tabs into per-project spaces with sync. TulipLot keeps a fixed grid of sites rendered live. What each one is for, and what each one costs.
- [How to view multiple websites at once](https://tuliplot.com/blog/view-multiple-websites-at-once/): Five ways to see two or more websites at the same time: split screen, browser windows, extensions, and a fixed dashboard grid. When each is the right call.
- [What is a browser start page (and do you still need one)?](https://tuliplot.com/blog/what-is-a-browser-start-page/): Start pages, home pages, and new-tab pages are three different things. Here's what each one does, why iGoogle's descendants keep dying, and what replaced them.

- [Why we built TulipLot](https://tuliplot.com/blog/why-we-built-tuliplot/): Tab overload is a workflow problem, not a willpower problem. Why we think a fixed grid beats a wall of tabs — and what we deliberately left out.
